citation.title: Estimation Methods for Nonhomogeneous Regression Models: Minimum Continuous Ranked Probability Score versus Maximum Likelihood
citation.authors: Gebetsberger, M.; Messner, J. W.; Mayr, G. J.; Zeileis, A.

topic: Probabilistic regression in weather postprocessing: CRPS versus log-score (maximum likelihood) estimation and distribution tail misspecification
own_question: When and why do CRPS-minimizing and LS-minimizing estimates differ for symmetric forecast distributions?
actual_method_and_evidence: Nonhomogeneous Gaussian, logistic and Student-t regression for ECMWF ensemble 2-m temperature at 11 central European stations. The models use tenfold random cross validation. A simulation with logistic truth and 1000 repeats is also reported. The authors report estimator discrepancies and W-shaped PIT histograms under Gaussian assumptions, with smaller differences for heavier-tailed models. In the correctly specified simulation, LS was slightly more efficient. No plasma, CES or timing content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: If the CRPS and log-score fits differ, or the PIT shape departs from uniform, this can indicate that the assumed predictive-distribution tails are misspecified. This holds in the authors' temperature-postprocessing setting.
claim_checks.qualification: Weather temperature case with a simulation. Interpretation specific to symmetric distributions. Not shown for CES.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. The inputs are ensemble mean and SD for fixed lead-time weather forecasts. This is future prediction, not current-report nowcasting.
validation_if_relevant: Random tenfold cross validation, assuming temporal independence. The simulations have a known truth.
forbidden_inferences: Do not imply that CRPS or LS training performs better for CES nowcasting.
Do not imply that Student-t or logistic tails suit CES temperature.
Do not cite this paper as plasma or real-time evidence.
Do not cite this paper as justifying random-split validation for our time series.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include only if our theory section discusses probabilistic scoring or estimation choices for uncertainty outputs. Otherwise exclude, because it is outside the scope of the intro.
